title: Ribollita
subtitle: Tuscan bread and cavolo nero soup
excerpt: The great Tuscan bean soup thickened with stale bread, layered with cavolo nero, cannellini beans, and root vegetables. Ribollita means reboiled, it is made in advance and the flavour deepens on the second day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ribollita is a quintessential Florentine cucina povera dish, the word means reboiled, referring to the tradition of making a large pot of bean soup, then adding stale bread to thicken it and reheating it over several days. It originated as a way to make the most of leftover minestrone and bread. The essential ingredient is cavolo nero, also called Tuscan kale or lacinato kale.

content.text: Ribollita is a commitment in the best way. Make it a day ahead, refrigerate it, and reheat it the following day, the flavours knit together and the bread becomes part of the structure rather than just a thickener. If you cannot find cavolo nero, Savoy cabbage is the closest substitute. Use the best olive oil you have for finishing; this is one of the dishes where it matters.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery, and carrot for 12 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and herbs and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add half the cannellini beans and the stock. Simmer for 15 minutes. Remove the herb sprigs.
Use a stick blender or masher to partially puree the soup, leave it about half chunky. Add the remaining whole beans and the cavolo nero. Cook for 15 minutes.

Add the torn bread and stir well. The bread will absorb the liquid and the soup will become very thick. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 10 more minutes. Remove from the heat and rest for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate overnight.
Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Serve in bowls with a very generous drizzle of olive oil and black pepper.
